title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-12
notes:
West leads the ♠K against 4♥. The defense begins by cashing 2 rounds of spades. West continues a third round of spades, ruffed by East. East returns a trump. The contract depends on South avoiding a diamond loser.

South will need to depend on the diamond finesse. East will have to have the ♦K. If East has a doubleton ♦K, South must play a low diamond to the ♦J and cash the ♦A on the second round. If East has 4 diamonds it will be necessary to assume that West has a doubleton ♦10. In this case, the ♦Q will have to be played on the first or second round of the suit to pin the ♦10.

In order to discover how to play diamonds, South should attempt to get a count on the hand. East's heart return should be won in the closed hand to preserve the ♥A as a later entry to the dummy.

South should next cash another round of trump in the closed hand, noting West's discard on the second round. South continues by cashing the ♣K, playing a club to the ♣A, and playing dummy's third club, ruffing in the closed hand.

When West follows to this trick, he is known to have started with 6 spades, 1 heart, and at least 3 clubs. West cannot have 4 diamonds and East's ♦K must be well guarded. After crossing to the ♥A, South knows enough about the distribution to lead the ♦Q from the dummy, in hopes of pinning the ♦10 in West's hand.
